items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 35:1
items.html: The seven corrections of the Galgalta are, by their initials, GT, KRA, PH — namely: the Galgalta, Tal deBdolcha, the membrane of the Avir, Rava deRavin, pure wool, the opening of the eyes, and the nose. Explanation: Correction 1: the Galgalta of Arich Anpin is corrected in the aspect of a white head, meaning that there is no hue of judgment in it whatsoever, and it is entirely mercy. For it is corrected in the aspect of the MEM of Tzelem, through the raising of the tops of the thighs of the NHY of Atik, as in Answer 11 above, see there. Correction 2: it is Tal deBdolcha, which is the Sealed Brain of Arich Anpin, and it is the principal head of Arich Anpin that extends from above downward in the aspect of a body. For the Galgalta and the Sealed Brain are the male and female of the head, coming from the two records of clothing and coarseness that are included one in the other, as in the Inner Observation, Page 440, Item 8, see there. And since the stature of the Galgalta comes principally from the record of clothing, there is no extension from it into the body, but only from the Sealed Brain, which comes from the record of coarseness. And it is called dew, because there is in it the root of the HaVaYaH of the fillings of Alephs, which means the aspect of the second restriction. For the membrane of the Avir, which is the aspect of the screen of the second restriction, has no rule over the Galgalta of Arich Anpin, because it was corrected in the aspect of the closed MEM, which is the aspect of the first three of Bina, over which no screen and restriction rules; and the beginning of the power of the screen of the second restriction begins to operate upon the Sealed Brain, and this membrane was made in the secret of the firmament that separates between the Galgalta and the Sealed Brain, for it brought out the Sealed Brain in the aspect of lower waters, as the Rav wrote above (Page 327, Item 72). Thus the beginning of the power of the second restriction is inscribed in the Sealed Brain, and hence the root of the HaVaYaH of the fillings of Alephs is hinted at in it. Also, it is known that the Malchut of the first restriction was concealed in RADLA, and in Arich Anpin there are only nine Sefirot (as above, Page 302, Items 14-15), so the HET is found missing relative to RADLA. And these two are hinted at in the aspect of dew, for Yud, Hei, Vav, Hei is in Gematria 45, and with the absence of the HET it is in Gematria 'tal' (39). This indicates the two new things that were renewed in the Sealed Brain: first, that the HET was removed from it and it has only nine Sefirot; second, that it is the first root that was imprinted from the screen of the second restriction, which is the filling of Alephs, as above. Hence it is called Tal. And it is called Bdolcha, for the clothing of the Gevura of Atik within it. For this Gevura is the aspect of the HET of the first restriction, concealed in RADLA, whose power is revealed in Atik only from above downward — that is, in the body of Atik, and in the aspect of the left line within it, namely in Gevura and Hod. And the Gevura is clothed in the Sealed Brain, only not in it in the aspect of a coupling, but in concealment; for this reason it has only nine Sefirot, since the Malchut of the first restriction is not in it in the aspect of a coupling, as above. And this Gevura of Atik, concealed in the Sealed Brain, is the root of all the Gevurot of Atzilut, from which comes the secret of the heating and the cooking of the seed, as in Answer 12, see there — meaning, only the aspect of preparation for the raising of the female waters, but there is no aspect of coupling upon it, see there. Hence it is like good wine upon its lees, for it rests upon its lees, since the power of this Malchut in the Gevura of Atik is not revealed in it at all. Therefore it is called 'Tal deBdolcha,' from the verse 'like the appearance of bdellium,' for the head of Arich Anpin is entirely mercy, and there is no hue of judgment in it, as is known. However, this Gevura of Atik, concealed in it in secrecy, makes in it an aspect of a glimmer of colors, like the bdellium, which is white yet colors glimmer in it; but in its essence it is entirely white, as explained — for it rests upon its lees. Hence it is called the dew of bdellium: it is called 'dew' for two matters — first, to indicate that it is missing Malchut and is only in the aspect of YHV; second, to indicate that it is the first receiver of the aspect of the correction of the second restriction, and hence it is in the filling of Alephs, which is in Gematria 'tal.' And it is called 'bdellium' for the concealment within it of the Gevura of Atik, which is the root of the Gevurot, hidden within it; and hence, although it is entirely white, there is still a glimmering of colors in it, like the bdellium.
